ground_truth.title: Learn graphic design
ground_truth.main_content:
Shape your career in graphic design with online courses and programs. Gain creative problem-solving and communication skills while mastering design software used across industries.

What is graphic design?

Graphic design is the digital fusion of art and advertising. It's everywhere — from the signs guiding us through forest trails to the websites we browse and the logos corporations use.

Graphic designers combine text and imagery to create visuals that convey messages, guide behavior, and promote products. These professionals have a keen eye for aesthetics, strong attention to detail, a knack for storytelling, and proficiency with design software.

Why learn graphic design online?

If you've ever wanted to demystify the magic behind dynamic digital ads, persuasive posters, beautiful billboards, or eye-popping packaging, consider learning graphic design online.

Learning graphic design online can help you:

- Become a graphic designer: Build the technical skills and gain the experience you need to pursue a career in graphic design.
- Perfect your personal branding: Learn how to develop a compelling personal brand and create visually appealing logos, banners, and portfolio materials.
- Bring creative ideas to life: Acquire the practical skills graphic designers use to take ideas from dreams to reality.
- Learn valuable software skills: Get acquainted with key graphic design programs like Adobe InDesign, Adobe Illustrator, and Figma.

What you will learn

The contents of graphic design courses and programs vary by skill level and institution. However, you can expect to learn the following foundational skills in most graphic design courses and programs online:

- The basics of color theory
- Visual communication and storytelling
- Understanding a client's needs and target audience
- Typography fundamentals
- Accessibility in design
- Design thinking: Ideation, iteration, and communication
- Data visualization
- Delivering a visual presentation or pitch
- User experience (UX) and user interface (UI) design
- Human-centered design techniques

Online graphic design courses vs. certificates vs. degrees

Once you decide on your specialty and industry, you may choose a graphic design program that aligns with your skills, professional and academic background, and preferred learning style.

Below, find pathways you can take to learn graphic design that span from online classes to advanced degree programs:

Courses

Online edX graphic design courses are short, flexible, self-paced programs that focus on specific topics. In 2–6 weeks, you can gain insight into the latest trends in graphic design or develop skills with industry-specific tools. edX offers free access to graphic design courses, with an optional upgrade that includes an official certificate of completion, graded assessments, and unlimited access to course materials.

Professional certificates

Professional certificate programs can help you build career-ready skills in graphic design in 2–10 months. These structured, multi-course programs combine practical training with foundational lessons. Upon completion, you'll earn a verified certificate from a leading university or institution.

Executive education

Executive education programs are for professionals who want to hone their leadership skills without pausing their careers. In 6–8 weeks, you'll take expert-led courses from top universities and explore industry case studies alongside fellow professionals.

Degrees

An online bachelor's degree program can provide you with a foundation in design principles and help you build a professional portfolio. Employers tend to prefer professionals with a bachelor's degree. According to CareerOneStop, 60% of graphic design professionals hold a bachelor of arts (BA) or a bachelor of fine arts (BFA) degree.

If you want advanced design knowledge or wish to pursue senior-level roles, earning your master of fine arts (MFA) degree may be a good choice. You can earn a BA, BFA, or MFA degree online.

Jobs to consider after learning graphic design online

Graphic designers create brand identities, enhance customer experience, and communicate ideas visually in the technology, education, fashion, healthcare, publishing, retail, and entertainment industries.

As a graphic designer, you could specialize in:

- Branding
- Advertising
- Illustration
- UI and UX design
- Experiential design (exhibitions and wayfinding)
- Motion graphics and animation
- Packaging design
- Publication and typographic design
- Web design

Consider some of the careers you can pursue with a degree in graphic design, with salary data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS):

Graphic designer

Graphic designers collaborate with copywriters to create visuals for marketing, publishing, and digital platforms. Experienced graphic designers may advance to senior designer or art director roles. Certifications in graphic design software may help you qualify for new career opportunities.

Required education: Bachelor's degree in graphic design or fine arts
BLS median annual salary (2024): $61,300

Art director

Art directors shape and oversee the visual style of media projects, packaging, and publications by working with teams to achieve cohesive designs. In addition to traditional media, art directors may coordinate graphics for websites, mobile platforms, and digital content design.

Required education: Bachelor's degree in art or design subjects
BLS median annual salary (2024): $111,040

Digital designer

Digital designers create visuals for digital media, apps, and websites. They are in demand in the tech and e-commerce industries, with opportunities to advance into UI/UX roles with certifications.

Required education: Bachelor's degree in digital design, graphic arts, or web design
BLS median annual salary (2024): $95,380

Desktop publisher

Desktop publishers design print and digital page layouts, often collaborating with other teams. Additional certifications in design-related areas may increase job opportunities.

Required education: Associate's degree in graphic design or graphic communications
BLS median annual salary (2024): $53,620

FAQs about graphic design

Can I learn graphic design on my own?

You can learn graphic design on your own through edX's online courses, professional certificate programs, executive education programs, and degree programs. These programs cover graphic design fundamentals, the latest insights, and the technology necessary for a career in the field.

How do I train to be a graphic designer?

To become a graphic designer, consider earning a bachelor's or master's degree in graphic design or fine arts. While studying, be sure to gain experience through internships or freelance projects to begin building a professional portfolio. You can become a graphic designer without a degree, but employers tend to prefer candidates with at least a bachelor's degree in graphic design or a related field.

Which type of graphic design is most in demand?

The BLS projects jobs for digital designers in graphic design — including UI, UX, motion graphics, and branding — to grow by 7% from 2024 to 2034, making it one of the most in-demand graphic design specializations. The BLS states that this increase is driven by the growth of e-commerce and the demand for mobile-first products and services as businesses prioritize digital presence and user experience.

Do graphic designers make good money?

According to BLS data, the median annual salary for graphic designers was $61,300 in May 2024. The lowest 10% earned less than $37,600, and the highest 10% earned more than $103,030. Salaries may vary based on your role, experience, industry, specialization, and location.
